newsitem.title: USA: Country music's Carl Perkins undergoes surgery.
newsitem.headline: Country music's Carl Perkins undergoes surgery.

text.p: Carl Perkins, who wrote the country-rock classic "Blue Suede Shoes," was reported in satisfactory condition on Monday following surgery to clear an artery.

"I made it through the surgery because I had the best doctors in the world and I would like to thank everyone who prayed for me," the 65-year-old entertainer said in a statement released by Baptist Memorial Hospital.
Perkins underwent angioplasty to clear a carotid artery. Such arteries in the neck and head supply blood to the brain, and a blockage can lead to a stroke.
Perkins entered the hospital for tests one week ago.

Perkins, who overcame a battle with throat cancer four years ago, sold more than two million copies of "Blue Suede Shoes" when he wrote and recorded it on the Memphis-based Sun label four decades ago. Elvis Presley recorded the song later and sold millions more.

Perkins received the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences "Hall of Fame" award for the song in 1986, and with the likes of Chuck Berry and Little Richard, is considered one of the founders of rock 'n' roll.
The rockabilly legend was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1987.
Perkins wrote the Johnny Cash classic "Daddy Sang Bass," as well as a number of songs recorded by the Beatles, including "Matchbox" and "Honey Don't."
His new album, "Go, Cat, Go," features collaborations with ex-Beatle George Harrison, Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers, Willie Nelson and John Fogerty.
